newsitem.title: GERMANY: VW says Q1 results above year-ago levels.
newsitem.headline: VW says Q1 results above year-ago levels.

text.p: German carmaker Volkswagen AG said on Thursday that its results in the 1997 first quarter were better than year-ago results.
"We do not make our quarterly results public but I can say that our results were better than last year," Volkswagen chief executive Ferdinand Piech told the group's annual news conference.
VW earlier on Thursday said sales for the first three months of 1997 were up 9.5 percent to 1.033 million vehicles from 943,000 vehicles in the 1995 first quarter.

Piech also reaffirmed the carmaker still had a goal of a pre-tax return on sales of 6.5 percent by the turn of the century. VW had a 1996 pre-tax return on sales of two percent, up from 1.3 percent in 1995 and 0.6 percent in 1994.
Piech declined to say if a news report that VW's profits had doubled in the first quarter was correct, but noted that a strike by Spanish truckers in February had cost the company 64 million marks.
